transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2025-04-04 16:00 PDT
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Sofia Martinez (Redwood AE), Daniel Cho (Redwood SE), Aisha Khan (VeloxCloud Partner Lead), Mark Rivera (VeloxCloud Sales), Tom Brooks (VeloxCloud Solutions Engineer)

Summary: quick pipeline review, focus Acme Retail, Baltic Bank, Mediflow. Align on owners and next steps.

00:00 Sofia (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call?
00:06 Aisha (VeloxCloud): Aisha here.
00:07 Mark (VeloxCloud): Mark on the line.
00:09 Tom (VeloxCloud): Tom, yep.
00:11 Daniel (Redwood SE): Daniel here.
00:12 Sofia: Great. Agenda — quick pipeline status, key risks, who owns next steps, and any blockers for next week.
00:23 Aisha: Sounds good. We want to focus on Acme Retail first, that's the highest priority for co-sell.
00:30 Sofia: Perfect. Daniel, you did initial perf notes for Acme?
00:33 Daniel: Yeah, I ran their sample trace against our hosted endpoint and a dedicated config. The hosted can meet baseline but when they hit 200 rps burst it's flaky, cost is higher. Dedicated is predictable. I noted latency delta — median token latency ~45ms hosted vs ~30ms on dedicated with batching enabled, but that's under ideal KV cache conditions. Some of the numbers in my doc are a bit noisy because of env variance.
01:05 Mark: Our ask from Acme is SLOs — 100ms p95 and predictable month-to-month spend. They care about cost per thousand tokens and also the ability to do private deployment later.
01:20 Sofia: Ok that maps to Redwood Dedicated offering. We can present two tracks: hosted trial for quick POC (fast start) or Dedicated reserved capacity for production guarantees. Pricing differs obviously.
01:34 Aisha: For the pitch, can we get a joint price range? Acme wants to see ballpark committed cost for a 6–12 month commit.
01:42 Sofia: Yes, we'll share a co-sell worksheet. I'll include a mid-range committed monthly figure and an on-demand hosted comparator.
01:49 Daniel: Also we should propose an SLA fallback plan: if Dedicated is delayed they can spin on hosted with throttling and auto-burst rules. Note: Acme has internal compliance about data retention — they prefer KMS with customer-managed keys.
02:10 Tom: That KMS requirement is a showstopper for them unless we can do a private VPC or bring-your-own-key, also they asked about audit logs and SOC2.
02:21 Sofia: Redwood supports KMS integrations and audit logs. For private key import and on-prem, that's in Redwood Private. We'll need to map the cost delta.
02:32 Aisha: Good. Who will own the intro to Acme technical contact for the deep dive?
02:36 Mark: I can set that up.
02:38 Aisha: Great.
02:40 Sofia: Daniel, can you run a tech deep-dive with Acme and include benchmark config and cost modeling?
02:45 Daniel: Yep, I'll schedule. I want to run a more thorough benchmark — p95 and p99 at peak load, with caching turned on and off, and a quantized model variant test. Expect to need about 48–72 hours to get meaningful numbers once they share sample traffic.
03:05 Mark: Timeline there? Acme wants procurement decision in 6 weeks.
03:09 Sofia: That's tight but doable if we turn around the trial in 2 weeks and have pricing ready.

03:25 Sofia: All right, next — Baltic Bank. Aisha, what's the status?
03:30 Aisha: Baltic Bank is in late evaluation. They flagged data residency (EU only), strict encryption, and third-party audit proof. There's also competition from AWS and an incumbent local provider.
03:45 Daniel: We did a quick mapping — Redwood Private can be deployed in the bank's VPC in eu-west-1 region, with HSM/KMS key integration and longer retention controls. But timeline for on-prem or private control plane setup is 6–8 weeks minimum depending on their security team approvals.
04:05 Tom: Pricing will be bigger because they need reserved capacity and possibly a dedicated private cluster. They also want performance proofs for tile-based models — they mentioned 'SageMaker' and Anthropic use cases.
04:22 Sofia: Competitor motion noted. How confident are we on procurement? Who is our sponsor?
04:28 Aisha: The sponsor is Priya Sharma in procurement + CTO level engagement from Andris. Priya is focused on cost predictability and legal terms.
04:36 Mark: I can help get the procurement thread moving. We need a joint exec briefing to show TCO vs the incumbent and highlight compliance packages.
04:45 Sofia: Agreed. Let's plan a joint exec briefing next week. Aisha, can you intro Priya to us?
04:50 Aisha: Yes, I'll send the intro by EOD tomorrow.
04:52 Sofia: Add to action items. Also we'll attach SOC2 cert and data residency attestation.
05:00 Daniel: One technical note — Baltic Bank asked about KV cache persistence and disaster recovery. We'll need to show how KV cache is replicated and how failover works in Dedicated. I'll draft a tech note.
05:15 Tom: Also they want audit logs exported to their SIEM (Splunk). Is that supported?
05:20 Sofia: Yes, Redwood Console can export logs; we'll provide an integration guide.

05:35 Sofia: Third deal is Mediflow — healthcare provider. Aisha, short color?
05:40 Aisha: Mediflow is small but regulated. They require HIPAA-like controls, potential on-prem option, and a POC first. The main ask is a POC for redaction and PHI handling plus integration with their internal EHR.
05:55 Daniel: For healthcare POCs we must confirm BAAs and ensure PHI handling pipeline. Redwood Private or Dedicated with strict KMS is recommended. We should confirm if they need full on-prem as an absolute, because that adds time.
06:12 Mark: Mediflow is cost sensitive. They might start with a small hosted POC if we can sign a BAA, then expand to Private later.
06:20 Sofia: Action items — Tom can prepare an integration checklist for EHR + SSO and Daniel will outline minimal config for a HIPAA-safe POC.

06:35 Aisha: On the co-sell mechanics — VeloxCloud asks for a 15% referral margin on net new, and we'd like joint logos and case study rights. Is that acceptable?
06:45 Sofia: Redwood generally supports partner margins and co-marketing. We need legal to confirm the specific percentage and case study approvals can be governed by our partner agreement. I'll loop in partnerships/legal.
06:58 Mark: Also we need a simple co-sell one-pager and a joint playbook that lays out who owns what in the demo and procurement phases.
07:08 Sofia: We'll produce a one-pager and a short playbook. Good ask.

07:20 Daniel: Technical risk callouts — Acme: sample traffic availability, Baltic: data residency & audit, Mediflow: BAA and EHR integration. We should rank them by time-to-close: Acme (4–6 weeks), Baltic (6–10 weeks), Mediflow (POC then expansion 8–12 weeks).
07:42 Aisha: Agreed on timing.
07:45 Sofia: Any blockers from your side that would slow us down?
07:49 Tom: For Mediflow we need API specs from their EHR vendor (Epic/other) — they're getting that to us. For Baltic we need the procurement SOW template from Redwood legal.
08:02 Sofia: I'll push the SOW template.

08:10 Sofia: Let's recap next steps: we (Redwood) will send co-sell one-pager, pricing worksheet, SOC2 and data residency docs; Daniel will schedule and run Acme technical deep-dive and benchmarking; Velox will make intros to Baltic and Mediflow contacts; Tom will prepare Mediflow integration checklist.
08:33 Aisha: I'll also prepare a short partner slide to include value props and differentiation to help procurement.
08:38 Sofia: Perfect. Anything else?
08:42 Mark: One question — for Acme, they asked if Redwood supports function/tool calling style output (structured output) for our prompt pipelines. They want structured response for downstream systems.
08:55 Daniel: Yes we support function-calling like patterns and can output JSON schemas, though sometimes the transcription of schema examples in docs is older. I'll include a sample in the deep-dive.
09:08 Sofia: Great. If nothing else, we'll close. Thanks everyone — we'll circulate notes and action items right after.
09:15 Aisha: Thanks all.
09:17 Mark: Thanks.
09:18 Tom: Bye.

Notes on transcription quality: occasional misheard model names and acronyms (e.g., 'SageMaker' transcribed as 'Sage maker' in one place), some overlapping talk captured as single lines.

References/attachments mentioned during call:
- co-sell worksheet (to be shared)
- SOC2 certificate link (will attach)
- Redwood Dedicated outline and pricing playbook (link)
- Mediflow EHR integration notes (Velox to share)

Closing: next sync in 1 week or ad-hoc as intros progress.
